messages.subject: knitr and ggplot2
parts:
Hello,

I just discovered knitr as alternative to swerve and try to explore
whether to use it for my thesis or not. I'm using ggplot a lot, so it
would be important for me to make it work together.
Im principle the plotting works, however the opts() from ggplot are
not always regarded in the latex file I produce. As reported before my
legends are clipped if the names are too long, margins do not change
and apart from size I don't seem to be able to change any other
feature of the axis text. Are all the opts() in ggplot in theory
applicable within knitr or not?
Oh, and another question: can I remove the grey background behind all
the code chunks in the pdf?

Kind Regards
Sylvia

R Version: 2.14.1

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] knitr and ggplot2
parts:
Hi,

Could you make a reproducible example for opts()?

For legend clipping, you can try to run knit() in an interactive R
session; currently there seems to be a bug with the pdf() device in R,
and I'm not sure if this can be fixed in the next version of R.

They gray background can be removed by setting the chunk option
background=white: http://yihui.name/knitr/options

Regards,
Yihui

hjust=1))

parts:
On Wed, Feb 22, 2012 at 4:49 AM, Tippmann, Sylvia
<Sylvia....@fmi.ch> wrote:
> oh sorry, the myc is just a custom string of colours...

That is too bad. You should not expect other people to make extra
guess work. Especially after we have reminded you to provide a
reproducible example, you should have updated your code in the last
email. Well, even after I did some guess work, I do not see how this
problem is specific to knitr. I saw the same thing in ggplot2 without
using knitr, so you probably should go to ggplot2 mailing list to seek
help on arranging your legend.

> But how can I make the code be displayed in a nice way? Since I can not introduce \newline commands because it has to be executed..
> Is there a way to format the R code and still do not interfere with it's function?

What is a nice way? Why do you have to use \newline? If there are
blank lines in your R code, they will be preserved naturally. I do not
know what you mean by "interfere", but you may need to know more about
formatR first: https://github.com/yihui/formatR/wiki Otherwise you
just turn off formatting by tidy=FALSE, and knitr will not touch the
format of your code at all.
